windows.notes:
Security fixes. Updating is recommended.
- A job named on the command line (ucopy-cli run NAME) is always the saved job of that name, never a file of that name in the current folder. To run a job file, give its path: ./NAME.toml.
- Jobs run by the system (as SYSTEM or root) can no longer be made to write over other files through links put in the target folder by someone who can change it.
- Linux and Mac: jobs run as root are refused when their file could be changed by anyone but root. Saving such a job again fixes it.
- Reports, recovery sheets and restore guides are never written through a link put where they're saved.

macos.notes:
Fixes for disk images.
- An image of a disk that was interrupted now carries on where it stopped, instead of reading the whole disk again (which wears a failing disk). It first checks a few sectors, so another disk at the same place, or an image damaged since, is imaged again.
- An image that can't be opened is never carried on in a new, empty file.
- Image a disk: the snapshot option now says that free space isn't read.
